## Objective

Make the residency admission ladder *measurable*: every `routing_resident_prefix`
decision must report a numeric reusable prefix (`n_past_actual` / `reuse_ratio`)
when a resident slot owner exists, and an explicitly labelled reason when it
cannot — so AC4 rule (a) and AC7's resident-vs-evicted split become evaluable
instead of dead.

## Problem statement

In the 24 h AC4 window (`2026-10-27T10:17:00Z → 2026-10-28T10:17:00Z`) the usage
report shows `residency_decisions: 3607` with **measured ratio: 0 / no
measurement: 3607**. Every decision line carries `n_past_actual=none` /
`reuse_ratio=none`, including the 234 decisions whose `residency_source` is
`session_slot` (the session *does* own a slot). With no numeric ratio, AC4
rule (a) ("live reuse below `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio` = 0.5") can never
fire, so the deadline classifier collapses to rule (b) plus an "ambiguous"
bucket (22 scheduling-attributed, 57 ambiguous, 20 genuine GPU-speed misses of
99 events) and the 24 h verdict cannot be decided.

The root cause is structural, not a logging typo: on the deployed llama.cpp
b8782 build `/slots` no longer reports per-slot `context_tokens`, so rung 1 of
`resolve_resident_prefix` (`residency_source=measured`) is unreachable in
production. Rung 2 (`session_slot`, ownership known, size unknown) deliberately
sets `n_past_actual=None` with an internal `reuse_ratio=1.0` sentinel for the
gate; `_log_residency_decision` suppresses the ratio whenever `n_past` is
`None`, so the resident path logs `none` and the gate's optimistic 1.0 is never
exposed as data. The remaining sources (`non_resident` 1755, `unknown` 984,
`none` 5) are genuinely unmeasured but are also indistinguishable from the
resident case, so the report cannot tell "ladder cannot measure" from "no slot
to measure".

## Users

- **Proxy operator / on-call** — needs a defensible AC4 verdict and a working
  rollback signal.
  - *As the operator, I want each residency decision to carry a numeric reuse
    ratio, so a cold-prefill admission is visible in the log before it becomes
    a 120 s deadline cancellation.*
- **The 24 h verification item (`LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K`) and its classifier child
  (`LP-0MVQ4X1S30034BQ1`)** — need rule (a) to be evaluable.
  - *As the verification agent, I want measured ratios on resident admissions,
    so the scheduling-attributed split is computed from data rather than from
    rule (b) alone.*
- **Future thrash investigations** — need the residency section of the usage
  report to separate resident from evicted reuse.
  - *As a future investigator, I want the resident/evicted reuse table populated,
    so I do not re-derive warmth from predicted `cached_ratio`.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Measured prefix at admission.** When a session owns a local slot,
  `routing_resident_prefix` logs a **numeric** `n_past_actual` and the derived
  `reuse_ratio` (`min(n_past_actual, estimated_tokens) / estimated_tokens`),
  sourced from the best available measurement and labelled by a distinct
  `residency_source` value so the provenance is auditable (live snapshot vs
  last measured dispatch for that `(model, session)` pair).
- **AC2 — Unmeasured is explicit and distinguishable.** A decision that cannot
  be measured logs an explicit, closed-vocabulary reason (e.g.
  `measurement=unavailable:no_slot`, `unavailable:no_prior_measurement`,
  `unavailable:stale_view`) instead of a bare `reuse_ratio=none`. `none` alone
  must no longer be the only signal, and a non-measurement must never be logged
  as a numeric `0.0000` or `1.0000`.
- **AC3 — Regression tests.** Tests assert: (i) a `session_slot` admission with
  a prior measured dispatch emits a numeric `reuse_ratio` matching
  `min(last_total, estimated_tokens) / estimated_tokens`; (ii) the same
  admission with no prior measurement emits the explicit unmeasured reason, not
  `none`; (iii) a non-resident admission is labelled `unavailable:no_slot`;
  (iv) an invalidated measurement (eviction / slot reassignment / model switch)
  is not reused; (v) the emitted line stays parseable by
  `proxy-usage-analysis`'s `log_parser`.
- **AC4 — Usage report reflects the split.** `analyze_proxy_usage.py` parses the
  new fields and its `## Residency-aware admission` section reports the
  measured/unmeasured counts plus a per-reason unmeasured breakdown, so
  "decisions logged but all unmeasured" is a visible finding rather than a
  silent zero (AC7 of the parent). Backward compatibility with existing log
  lines is preserved.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** `proxy/docs/routing.md` (observability grammar),
  `docs/dev/resident-prefix-rollout.md` (what to read / known limits) and
  `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` describe the measurement sources, the
  closed unmeasured-reason vocabulary and the remaining limitation (buffered
  non-streaming dispatches carry no `prompt_progress` measurement).
- **AC6 — Re-run unblocked (handoff).** The measurement gap is closed on `dev`
  and the parent item `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K` is re-armed for a fresh
  restart-free 24 h window; the AC4 rule (a) classification is then evaluable.
  The soak itself is **not** part of this item.
- **AC7 — Suite green.** The full project test suite passes with the change
  (enforced by the dev-push gate; no ad-hoc full-suite runs).

## Constraints

- **No synchronous `/slots` call on the admission hot path.** llama-server holds
  `/slots` for >15 s while processing a prompt batch (`LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC`), so
  the measurement must come from already-captured state (cached snapshot or the
  in-process `measured_prefill` store).
- **Fail-open.** No measurement may ever deny local service or raise into the
  request path; the ladder keeps degrading one rung at a time.
- **Additive log grammar.** Existing consumers (`log_parser`,
  `proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py`) already assert
  `reuse_ratio=none` for genuine non-measurements (`LP-0MVNPZY22008B536`); extend
  the grammar with new fields/source values rather than repurposing `none`.
- **No fabricated numbers.** A stale or invalidated measurement must never be
  reported as a ratio — the failure mode this item exists to fix.
- **Scope.** Admission-decision measurement and observability only: no change to
  the residency *policy* (thresholds, tenancy bound, pricing rules) and no 24 h
  measurement run inside this item.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py::resolve_resident_prefix` — three-rung ladder
  (`measured` → `session_slot` → `non_resident`/`unknown`). Rung 1 needs
  `context_tokens` from the cached `/slots` snapshot
  (`proxy/proxy/residency.py`), which the deployed b8782 build no longer
  reports, so in production only rungs 2–3 fire.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py::_log_residency_decision` — emits the
  `routing_resident_prefix` line; suppresses `reuse_ratio` whenever
  `n_past_actual` is `None`, which is why 234 resident admissions log `none`.
- `proxy/proxy/measured_prefill.py` — `MeasuredPrefill` (`total`, `cache`,
  `processed`, `time_ms`, `measured_cached_ratio`, `measured_new_tokens`) plus
  `set_measured_prefill` / `get_measured_prefill` / `clear_measured_prefill`
  keyed by `(model, session)`, populated from llama-server's
  `prompt_progress` first event in `proxy/proxy/router.py` (~2275) when
  `server.local_measured_cache_abort_enabled` is on (it is: `proxy/config.yaml`
  ~2102). Delivered by `LP-0MVR7DAFF006HBRX` (completed).
  `clear_measured_prefill` currently has **no caller**, so a measurement is
  never invalidated today.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — `RE_REUSE_RATIO`
  matches `[\d.]+|none`; the residency branch maps `none` to `None`.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py::_append_residency_section`
  — counts `measured` as `reuse_ratio is not None`, so resident admissions land
  in "no measurement"; `aggregation.py` carries `residency_events`.
- Measurement window evidence and the AC4 classifier rule (a)/(b) live on
  `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K` / `LP-0MVQ4X1S30034BQ1`.

## Desired change

Populate the admission-time measurement, then make non-measurements
self-describing:

1. **New measurement rung between 1 and 2.** When the cached snapshot has no
   `context_tokens` but the session owns the slot, consult
   `measured_prefill.get_measured_prefill(model, session)`; the last dispatch's
   `total` is the prompt size llama-server last processed in that session's slot,
   i.e. the resident prefix size. Report it as `n_past_actual` with a new
   `residency_source` (e.g. `measured_last_dispatch`) and derive
   `reuse_ratio = min(total, estimated_tokens) / estimated_tokens`. The gate's
   internal `1.0` sentinel then becomes a real measurement rather than an
   assumption.
2. **Invalidate stale measurements.** Clear or reject a measurement when the
   session loses its slot, the slot is reassigned to another session, or the
   model changes — otherwise the fix trades one fabrication for another.
3. **Closed unmeasured vocabulary.** Emit an additive `measurement=` field with
   values such as `measured`, `unavailable:no_slot`,
   `unavailable:no_prior_measurement`, `unavailable:stale_view`,
   `unavailable:capture_disabled` (when
   `local_measured_cache_abort_enabled` is off), keeping
   `reuse_ratio=none` for the numeric-absent case so existing assertions and
   parsers stay valid.
4. **Report the breakdown.** Teach `log_parser` + `reporting` the new field so
   the residency section shows measured vs unmeasured-by-reason counts, and
   `aggregation` counters stay backward compatible with old log files.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — new measurement rung in `resolve_resident_prefix`;
  `ResidentPrefixFacts` gains a measurement-provenance/reason field;
  `_log_residency_decision` emits the additive `measurement=` field and no
  longer reports the `1.0` sentinel as if measured.
- `proxy/proxy/measured_prefill.py` — expose/guard the last-measurement lookup
  used at admission (and give `clear_measured_prefill` real callers).
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — invalidate the per-`(model, session)` measurement on
  eviction / slot release / model switch (capture point already here).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py` — AC3 regression tests
  (resident-with-measurement, resident-without, non-resident, invalidation,
  parseability).
- `proxy/tests/test_measured_prefill_capture.py` — store lookup/clear semantics.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — parse
  `measurement=`; keep `reuse_ratio=none` → `None`.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — residency section
  measured/unmeasured-by-reason counters.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — residency counters
  (if a new aggregate key is added).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — parser
  and report tests for the new field (old-format lines still parse).
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — observability grammar and measurement sources.
- `docs/dev/resident-prefix-rollout.md` — what to read, and the residual
  limitation for buffered dispatches.
- `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` — ladder/observability section update.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Stale measurement fabricates a ratio (highest risk).** A `(model, session)`
  measurement survives eviction and slot reassignment today. Mitigation: rung
  only when ownership is live, plus explicit invalidation and a test per
  invalidation path. Assumption: `total` of the last dispatch is an acceptable
  proxy for the slot's resident prefix (same prompt plus decode, so slightly
  conservative).
- **Buffered (non-streaming) dispatches emit no `prompt_progress`.** Sessions
  served only by buffered local dispatches stay unmeasured; AC2's explicit
  reason makes that visible. Assumption: local large-prompt traffic is
  streaming in practice (the early-abort path already assumes it).
- **Rollback interaction.** With `local_measured_cache_abort_enabled: 0` the
  store is never populated; all resident decisions become
  `unavailable:capture_disabled`. This is intended and documented, not a
  regression.
- **Grammar churn.** Adding `measurement=` risks breaking a consumer that
  parses the line positionally; mitigated by additive fields, parser tests over
  both old and new lines, and no change to existing key order.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Fixing attribution invites folding in the 24 h soak, a
  classifier rewrite, or policy tuning. Those stay with
  `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K` / `LP-0MVQ4X1S30034BQ1`; extra opportunities found
  during implementation are filed as linked items, not absorbed here.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` — epic: resident-prefix admission + session tenancy
  (AC5 observability is the parent of this log line).
- `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K` — 24 h AC4 verification; **blocked by** this item
  (verdict FAIL/not-pass, loops back after the fix).
- `LP-0MVQ4X1S30034BQ1` — window report counters and scheduling-attribution
  split (rule (a)/(b) classifier; consumes the new field).
- `LP-0MVNPZY22008B536` (completed) — suppressed the `0.0` sentinel for
  non-resident sessions; this item must not undo it.
- `LP-0MVN4LANP0069QQM` (completed) — made the fail-open (`unknown`) path log
  its decision; the `unavailable:stale_view` reason extends that work.
- `LP-0MVR7DAFF006HBRX` (completed) — measured prefill capture from
  `prompt_progress`; supplies the measurement source used here.
- `LP-0MVR7IN0O000DPXN` (completed) — early abort on measured cache deficit;
  same store, decision-path consumer.
- `LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC` — the `/slots` >15 s stall that forbids a synchronous
  query on the hot path.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

No producer questions were required: the item's seed context already carried the
problem, verbatim log evidence, the value distribution, the AC set and the
type/priority, and every remaining unknown was answerable by repository
inspection.

- Q: "Which measurement source can supply a numeric prefix at admission, given
  the deployed build no longer reports `context_tokens`?" — Answer (agent,
  repo research): the per-`(model, session)` store in
  `proxy/proxy/measured_prefill.py`, populated from llama-server's
  `prompt_progress` first event in `proxy/proxy/router.py` (~2275) and already
  enabled in `proxy/config.yaml` (`local_measured_cache_abort_enabled: true`).
  Its `total` is the prompt size last processed in that session's slot. Source:
  `docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` (§
  *What to read, what never to call*), `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (~2470–2635).
- Q: "Why does the resident (`session_slot`) path log `none` rather than the
  gate's `1.0`?" — Answer (agent, repo research): `_log_residency_decision`
  treats a `None` `n_past_actual` as "unmeasured" and suppresses the ratio,
  while `resolve_resident_prefix` keeps `reuse_ratio=1.0` purely as an internal
  gate sentinel for the restore path. Source: `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
  (`_log_residency_decision`, `resolve_resident_prefix`).
- Q: "Is the fix allowed to change the residency policy?" — Answer (agent,
  scope decision recorded on the item): no; policy thresholds stay as shipped
  and only measurement/observability changes. The 24 h re-measurement stays with
  `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K`. Source: this brief's Constraints and the parent item's
  AC4/AC7 wording.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVNPZY22008B536** – routing_resident_prefix logs reuse_ratio=0.0000 for non-resident sessions, so the usage report counts a non-measurement as a measured prefix (completed)
- **LP-0MVKU49K1002FJ2X** – Measure memory and page-cache pressure for N=8 session snapshots (blocked)

- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: abort, absent, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+376 more)

## Plan (feature decomposition)

Planned 2026-10-29 by the plan skill. Eight children, test-first, each a
minimal end-to-end slice. **Implementation order = dependency order**:
`LP-0MVT2PB6U007PKD1` → `LP-0MVT2PY3J00077W6` → `LP-0MVT2Q1SD009JLKD` →
`LP-0MVT2QFAP0082BKR` → `LP-0MVT2QHMU0008F2V` → `LP-0MVT2QW9P0054LX2` →
`LP-0MVT2QYXI0025U6C` (with `LP-0MVT2PF1C008LAPB` runnable in parallel from the
start), so a run of `/skill:implement LP-0MVRZXPH70025ZNR` walks `wl next`.

| # | Child | Type | Covers | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `LP-0MVT2PB6U007PKD1` — [test] xfail regression suite for admission-time residency measurement | task | AC3(i)–(iv) | S |
| 2 | `LP-0MVT2PF1C008LAPB` — [test] xfail suite for `measurement=` grammar and residency report breakdown | task | AC3(v), AC4 | S |

| 4 | `LP-0MVT2Q1SD009JLKD` — [impl] Closed unmeasured-reason vocabulary for residency decisions | feature | AC2 | M |

# Intake brief: join hard-wrapped AC bullets in tree_coverage extraction

## Goal (user story)

As a planner/auditor agent — or the producer reading its coverage report — I want `extract_acceptance_criteria()` to return a hard-wrapped AC bullet as one complete sentence, so the parent↔child AC coverage review compares whole requirements instead of truncated fragments and stops producing a false `stop` / 0 % coverage verdict on well-maintained, wrapped items.

## Problem statement

`extract_acceptance_criteria()` treats every physical line of an `## Acceptance Criteria` section as a separate AC, so a bullet hard-wrapped at ~80 columns is cut at its first line. Both sides of the parent↔child comparison are truncated the same way, parent↔child Jaccard scores collapse to 0.05–0.18 (below the 0.2 auto-close floor), and `run_coverage_review()` answers `recommendation: "stop"` with 0 % coverage for items whose children demonstrably cover the scope.

## Users

- **Planner and intake agents (downtime-dispatched, no interactive approver).** As a planner agent, I want the AC coverage helper to read whole ACs, so a wrapped item is not held at `intake_complete`/`plan_complete` by a parsing artefact and I do not have to override the helper with a hand-built per-AC table.
- **Producer / operator reviewing stage advancement.** As the producer, I want a `stop` recommendation to mean a real coverage gap, so I can trust the gate instead of re-verifying every wrapped item by hand.
- **Auditors.** As the audit skill, I want the coverage evidence to reflect requirement text, so coverage percentages and gap-conflict messages are meaningful.

## Acceptance criteria

- `extract_acceptance_criteria()` returns one AC entry per top-level bullet, joining the bullet's wrapped continuation lines into that entry: a bullet spanning N physical lines yields exactly one string containing the full sentence, with intra-entry whitespace collapsed to single spaces.
- Continuation joining inserts a single space between wrapped lines except where the previous line ends with a hyphen attached to the preceding word (`high-` + `priority`, `per-` + `request`), which is rejoined without a space; a hyphen preceded by whitespace keeps the space.
- Existing extraction semantics are preserved unchanged: deeper-indented sub-list markers are still excluded as ACs and their text is not appended to the parent AC; a blank line ends the current AC entry (an unmarked prose paragraph after a blank line is not merged into it); lines inside a fenced code block and table rows are not appended; unwrapped single-line bullets and ordered items (`1.`, `1)`) extract exactly as they do today.
- Scope and invariants preserved: `compute_coverage()`, `jaccard_similarity()`, `resolve_coverage_gaps()`, the 0.4 coverage threshold and the 0.2 auto-close floor are unchanged, and the fail-closed path in `run_coverage_review()` still returns `recommendation: "stop"` with the existing warning when an AC section yields no parseable entry (existing fail-closed tests pass unmodified).
- Regression tests cover, at minimum: one hard-wrapped multi-line bullet yielding one complete AC; mixed wrapped and unwrapped bullets plus a wrapped ordered item; a wrapped bullet that contains a nested sub-list (sub-list excluded, parent text complete); a hyphen-broken word rejoined without a space; a blank-line-terminated entry not over-merged; and the untouched existing `TestExtractAcceptanceCriteria` cases.
- Re-running `run_coverage_review()` on `LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD` after the fix records a before/after per-AC best-match score table in a comment on this item, showing the score movement (pre-fix 0.053–0.182 measured during intake; expected post-fix 0.115–0.389) with at least two of the five parent ACs clearing the 0.2 auto-close floor, so the review no longer resolves zero of five gaps.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change: the `extract_acceptance_criteria()` docstring states the continuation-join and hyphen rules, and any doc that describes per-line AC semantics is corrected (no `docs/` page currently documents extraction; `skill/intake/SKILL.md` and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` reference only `apply_coverage_review`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` included; run through `/skill:test`).

## Constraints

- The change is extraction-only: `compute_coverage()`, `jaccard_similarity()`, `resolve_coverage_gaps()`, the 0.4 coverage threshold and the 0.2 auto-close floor are untouched. Threshold or tokenisation tuning is a separate item if the post-fix signal is still too weak.
- Fail-closed behaviour is preserved: an AC section that yields no parseable entry still returns `recommendation: "stop"` with the existing warning message.
- The fix lands in the framework repo `SorraAgents` (`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py`), while this work item lives in the `llm` worklog — the implementing commit hash must be recorded in a comment here, and the implement phase must work in the SorraAgents checkout, not beneath `~/projects/llm`.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill`, so edits take effect immediately for every agent; the change must therefore be correct and tested in one pass (no partial behaviour left live).
- Unit tests must remain hermetic — fixtures inline in the test module, no `wl` subprocess and no dependency on another project's live worklog store for CI.
- Scope-creep guard: re-working the coverage report format, semantic matching, or stop-word handling is explicitly out of scope.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (1,092 lines): `extract_acceptance_criteria()` scans the AC section line by line, strips `- ` / `+ ` / `N.` / `N)` markers via `_strip_ac_list_marker()`, and appends each marker line as one AC; non-marker lines are ignored entirely (function at line 374). Nested-indent exclusion was added in `7b1aeece` (SA-0MVO7R2WU0058RNJ), which also added the fail-closed path.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — `TestExtractAcceptanceCriteria` holds the 20 existing extraction cases (nested bullet vs numbered, indented section, multi-digit numbering, bold-led items, document order). No wrapped-bullet case exists.
- Consumers: `run_coverage_review()` / `apply_coverage_review()` are called by the intake and plan skills; no other module imports the extractor.
- Measured on `LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD` (5 wrapped parent ACs, 3 children) during this intake, with a prototype that joins continuation lines:

| Parent AC | Best match now | Best match with join | 0.2 auto-close floor |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| AC1 (≥24 h window numbers) | 0.182 | 0.250 | cleared |
| AC2 (idle-admitted percentiles) | 0.077 | 0.115 | still below |
| AC3 (denials / timeouts) | 0.056 | 0.118 | still below |
| AC4 (interactive tier) | 0.053 | 0.152 | still below |
| AC5 (enable / tuning decision) | 0.158 | 0.389 | cleared |

  The prototype also reproduced the join hazard behind the hyphen rule: `high-
priority` joined with a space yields `high- priority`.
- The pre-fix review of that item resolved 0 of 5 gaps (`recommendation: "stop"`, `coverage_pct: 0.0`, best-match scores 0.05–0.18) and had to be overridden manually with an evidence table (comment `LP-C0MVSB1GR6007O3EN`).

## Desired change

Accumulate continuation lines into the open AC entry instead of discarding them: when a line inside the AC section carries no list marker, is not blank, is not a heading, and is not inside a fenced code block, append it to the current AC with the join rule above (single space, or no space after a word-attached hyphen) and normalise whitespace. Flush the accumulated entry on the next top-level marker, a blank line, or the end of the section. Nested markers keep their current "ignored, not promoted, not appended" behaviour. Update the docstring to state these rules.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — `extract_acceptance_criteria()` and `_strip_ac_list_marker()`; continuation accumulation plus docstring (SorraAgents repo)
- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — new wrapped-bullet regression cases in `TestExtractAcceptanceCriteria`
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — only if the coverage-review description needs a note (currently delegates to `apply_coverage_review`)
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — same, verify no per-line semantics are described

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — blank line terminates an entry.** Hard-wrapped bullets are contiguous in practice; treating a blank line as an entry boundary keeps stray prose out of ACs and matches the "wrapped bullet" root cause. Consequence: a bullet with an intentional blank line inside it is read as two fragments of one AC.
- **Assumption — hyphen rule is `word-` immediately followed by the continuation**, i.e. no whitespace before the hyphen. `text -` (spaced dash) keeps the separating space.
- **Assumption — "no longer reports all 5 as uncovered"** is measured as score movement plus resolved-gap count (2 of 5 at the 0.2 floor), not as `coverage_pct` at the 0.4 threshold. With the fix alone `coverage_pct` stays 0 % for that item because AC2–AC4 remain below 0.4; reaching `proceed` needs scoring work that is out of scope.
- **Risk — over-merging.** A prose paragraph or note between bullets could be appended to the previous AC; mitigated by the blank-line/heading/fence boundaries and by a dedicated regression test.
- **Risk — silent behaviour change for consumers.** Intake and plan both gate on this helper, so a malformed join would wrongly advance or block stages; mitigated by keeping the full existing test class green and adding the mixed/nested cases.
- **Risk — cross-repo traceability.** The item is tracked in `llm` but the code is in `SorraAgents`; a missing commit reference would make the fix unauditable.
- **Scope-creep risk:** better coverage discrimination (stop words, thresholds, semantic similarity) is tempting once the numbers are visible — record it as a linked follow-up item, not in this change.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD` — Measure idle-aware local admission impact over ≥24h (before/after): the item whose coverage review produced the false `stop`; it is now `plan_complete` with manual per-AC evidence.
- `LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF`, `LP-0MVRCLPVI0057116`, `LP-0MVSAZLNL007B072` — the children used as the child-side corpus for the measurement above.
- `SA-0MVO7R2WU0058RNJ` (commit `7b1aeece`, SorraAgents) — previous change to the same function: nested-bullet AC promotion fix plus fail-closed on an unparseable AC section; established the test class and the indentation semantics preserved here.
- `LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E` — notes the same function in its planning context (numbered-AC extraction), showing this helper is a recurring source of false coverage signals.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer answers were obtained in this session (downtime dispatch, no interactive approver). The seed context was sufficient to draft the brief; the entries below record the interpretations the brief proceeds on.

- **OPEN QUESTION 1** (directed to the producer/operator; matters because it decides whether AC3 of this item is met by extraction alone): Does "no longer reports all 5 parent ACs as uncovered" mean the *resolved-gap* signal must move (scores above the 0.2 auto-close floor, `coverage_pct` at 0.4 unchanged), or must the 0.4-scored `coverage_pct` itself rise above 0 %?
  - **Assumption used:** the resolved-gap signal — the item's own parenthetical says "score movement is what matters, not a specific threshold", and raising the 0.4-threshold coverage would require scoring changes the root-cause analysis does not describe.
- **Q: Where does the extractor live and which tests cover it?** — Answer (research, no producer input needed): `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` in the framework repo `SorraAgents` (the item's `skills/...` path is the same tree, renamed `skill/`), with `TestExtractAcceptanceCriteria` in `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — not `skill/plan/tests/` as the item's Key Files suggested. Evidence: `grep -rn extract_acceptance_criteria skill/`, `git log -- skill/shared/tree_coverage.py`.
- **Q: Do wrapped ACs really explain the 0 % coverage, or is scoring also at fault?** — Answer (research): both sides are truncated, and joining both sides lifts best-match scores from 0.053–0.182 to 0.115–0.389 (table above), i.e. extraction is the primary defect; AC2–AC4 stay below the 0.4 threshold, which is scoring/tokenisation territory and out of scope. Evidence: prototype extraction run over `wl show` output for `LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD` and its three children.
- **Q: Is editing this agent-infrastructure file authorised?** — Answer (interpretation): yes for this item — it exists as a producer-filed bug with explicit ACs naming the function, so the item is the authorisation; any behaviour beyond continuation joining (thresholds, scoring) still needs its own item. Recorded so the producer can correct the reading at review.

Full untruncated automated report sidecar: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-LP-0MVSB0E7W003IMH4.md`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVF7KSJW007L2QF** – End-to-end integration test and regression gate (completed)
- **LP-0MVF7KO8C005NB59** – Quota hard stop and cost guard (completed)

- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: acceptance, acs, agent, already, also (+99 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: acceptance, acs, agent, already, also (+99 more)

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-29T05:03Z (plan, session `herdr-1793250095-1441524-3433`) — auto-plan path (`plan-if-needed` → `skip`, Effort Small / Risk Low): no child decomposition created; six automated review stages run against the existing content. Requirements & AC alignment review added one AC ("Scope and invariants preserved") promoting two existing Constraints (extraction-only change; fail-closed behaviour preserved) into testable criteria. # Intake brief: `prefill_eta_seconds` is an unlabelled cache-cold bound; the M3 accuracy metric compares it to a different population

discovered-from:LP-0MVGR2OXT0096OGK

## Problem statement

The published `prefill_eta_seconds` on `/llama/local/status` prices the *reference prompt, cache-cold* (`cached_ratio = 0.0`), while the proxy's own M3 metric compares it against llama-server `prompt eval time` — a distribution that, by construction, measures **only the uncached remainder** of mostly-warm prompts. Two stacked definitional offsets therefore make the report assert a calibration defect (`over_predicts`, +3137 % at p50) that the analysis skill's own REFERENCE.md already says is "expected". Either the signal is mislabelled for its consumers, or the metric is measuring the wrong thing — and today the operator cannot tell which, so the true calibration quality of the ETA (the number the admission guard enforces) is not measured at all.

## Evidence (measured, this machine)

**1. The published number is a cache-cold reference bound, not a per-request estimate.**

- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py::status_estimate` calls `projected_wait_seconds(model, tokens, 0.0, busy, ...)` — `cached_ratio` is hard-coded `0.0`, and `per_slot_prefill_eta_seconds` does the same. The estimate is therefore the *worst case* (nothing cached).
- `reference_tokens(model, config)` returns `_last_prompt_tokens[model]` — the **single most recent** dispatch's prompt size, uncapped (falls back to `local_admission_guard_reference_tokens`, default 32 000).
- Observed `status_request` polls on 2026-10-29 carry `prefill_eta_seconds=97.5`, i.e. 25 000 tok × 3.9 ms (the default `DEFAULT_PREFILL_MS_PER_TOKEN`) — below `CONSERVATIVE_MIN_TOKENS` (32 768), so the p75 uplift is *not* applied. Predicted p50 91.6 s ⇒ implied reference ≈ 23 500 tokens; p90 118.5 s ⇒ ≈ 30 400 tokens.
- One 119 K-token dispatch sets the reference to 119 K for every subsequent poll ⇒ a published bound of ≈ 464 s until the next dispatch, independent of the traffic actually arriving.

**2. Served traffic is dominated by warm, cache-served prompts.**

From `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` `dispatch_first_byte_ms` samples (n = 141, 2026-10-29):

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| `estimated_tokens` p50 / p90 | 11 226 / 20 268 |
| Warm dispatches (`cache_state=warm`) | 93 / 141 = **66 %**, `cached_ratio` p50 **0.957** |
| Warm new (uncached) tokens p50 | **521** |
| Cold (ratio 0.0) dispatches | 48, ms/new-token p50 2.05 / p90 3.55 |
| `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` p50 / p90 | **3 470 ms / 30 789 ms** |

**3. The observed comparison population is the uncached remainder only.**

From `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log` `prompt eval time = … ms / N tokens` (n = 185, same day):

| Quantile | ms | new tokens evaluated |
|---|---:|---:|
| p50 | 3 674 | **999** |
| p90 | 21 759 | 6 380 |
| p99 | 103 032 | 25 735 |

22 % of prompt-eval lines evaluate < 64 new tokens (e.g. `91.53 ms / 4 tokens`). A cache-warm continuation is *supposed* to record a tiny `prompt eval time`; comparing it with a 25 K-token cache-cold bound is not a calibration measurement.

**4. The metric's own documentation predicts the verdict it then reports as a defect.**

`REFERENCE.md` (Limitations): "The prediction is the cache-cold *reference-prompt* cost, so systematic over-prediction is expected when the reference prompt is larger than the median served prompt; read it as 'does the published ETA reflect the typical real prefill a dispatcher will face', not as a per-request calibration score." The report nevertheless renders **`(prefill ETA verdict: over_predicts)`** and the M2 sentence "**Prefill-ETA signal (`prefill_eta_seconds`): does not match reality.**"

**5. M3 cannot band or correct for any of this, because the log line lacks the context.**

`status_request` logs only `prefill_eta_seconds` / `queue_eta_seconds`. It does **not** log `prefill_eta_reference_tokens`, `prefill_eta_calibrated`, `prefill_eta_rate_bucket`, `prefill_eta_samples`, or the assumed `cached_ratio` — all of which `status_estimate` already computes internally. So `prefill_eta_error_json` compares a bound of unknown reference size against an unmatched population.

- **Risk (high): silent safety regression.** "Calibrating" the ETA to the reported observed distribution would make the guard admit cache-cold large prompts and waste GPU on guaranteed-loss prefills. Mitigation: the constraint above; the per-request guard path is explicitly out of scope and pinned by regression tests.
- **Risk (low): payload contract change breaks a dispatcher.** Q1 = option (a) keeps `prefill_eta_seconds` semantics and adds fields, so the change is additive for external dispatchers (herdr workers are the known readers). Mitigation: additive-only payload/log fields; the rejected option (b) — renaming/repurposing — is explicitly out of scope, and the field must document its semantics because it is currently documented nowhere outside the code.
- **Risk (medium): log-format drift breaks the analysis.** New fields must not disturb existing regexes/parsers. Mitigation: append-only, plus parser tests.
- **Risk (low): `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` is not `prompt eval time`.** It includes queue→first-byte overheads other than prefill; the matched comparison is still the closest same-dispatch observable and is the number the guard promises. Assumption recorded; the brief does not claim it equals llama-server's prompt-eval.
- **Risk (low): 24 h windows are noisy** (n ≈ 1 200 observed, ≈ 12 000 polls). Mitigation: thresholds are relation-based (bound holds / violates), not point estimates, and `inconclusive` is a legitimate outcome.
- **Scope-creep guard:** per-request query parameters on `/llama/local/status` (the rejected Q1 option (c)), prompt-size-banded calibration of the *published* field, and any change to the admission budget constants are **out of scope** for this item; if wanted later they become linked child items.
- **Assumption:** the 25 % two-sided tolerance in `PREFILL_ETA_MATCH_TOLERANCE_PCT` is meaningful only for matched pairs; a cache-cold bound is *expected* to exceed served durations, so it needs a one-sided "must not be violated" test instead (Q3).
- **Matched-join mechanics (verified at plan time, 2026-10-29).** The join key exists on both sides: `prefill_eta.record_guard_decision` emits `local_admission_guard … eta_prefill_s=<s> … new_tokens=<n> session=<id>` (line ≈ 1453) and the local dispatch records `dispatch_first_byte_ms=… dispatch_to_first_byte_ms=… session=<id> model=<model>` (`log_parser.RE_DISPATCH_TO_FIRST_BYTE`, `RE_SESSION`). Three consequences to handle (and to report, not to hide): (i) the guard is inert for uncalibrated buckets and logs nothing, and logs nothing in `observe` mode when the decision is inactive — such dispatches are **unmatched** and must be counted separately (`unmatched_dispatches`), never folded into the matched figure; (ii) `enforced=false` (observe policy) pairs are still valid *pricing* measurements — include them, but report the split so a rollout window is interpretable; (iii) use the guard's `eta_prefill_s` (own-prefill term, the per-request priced value), not `projected_wait_s` (which adds occupancy), or the matched error would price queueing the observed first byte already includes only once.

# Feature: local-preferred chain selection and deferral

Parent: LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY.

## Goal

Make `local-preferred` behave as "local-only while deferrable, remote-ok once the prompt is too large for local", on every exit path of both dispatch cycles.

## Deliverables

1. **Local-pinned while deferrable.** `apply_local_preference()` and the dispatch-loop choke point (`_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote`, both cycles) treat `local-preferred` exactly as today's `local-only`: no non-local dispatch on any exit — admission refusal, lease denial, slot exhaustion, context/`resident_prefix` skip, stall, empty response, sibling-failure.
2. **Deferral.** A deferrable request with no free local slot queues within `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`; on expiry it returns a **retryable** 429 via the existing truthful-timing helper (`_refusal_retry_timing`): `retryable: true`, `Retry-After`, `retry_at`, `X-Local-Route: refused`, plus the verdict from LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ. The request is *not* enqueued twice, no lease/slot is leaked, the response is stamped once.
3. **Too-large → remote-ok.** When the verdict is `too_large`, remove the local entry from the effective chain at resolution time (the existing `remote-ok` filtering path) so remote tiers serve the request with no deferral and no local-capacity 429.
4. **Alias.** `local-only` normalises to the same behaviour (LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16), including log lines.
5. **Logging.** One line per request naming the resolved preference and whether it was pinned, deferred or promoted to remote — so an operator can tell a deferral from chain exhaustion.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 With `local-preferred` and a deferrable verdict on *each* listed exit path, no remote dispatch occurs (asserted per path in tests).
- AC2 With `local-preferred` and a free local slot, the request is served locally as today.
- AC3 With `local-preferred` and a deferrable verdict after the queue budget, the response is 429 with `retryable: true`, a `Retry-After`/`retry_at` pair consistent with the refusal timing contract, `X-Local-Route: refused`, and a body verdict of `deferrable`.
- AC4 With `local-preferred` and a `too_large` verdict, the chain excludes local and a remote provider serves the request; no 429 is produced for local capacity.
- AC5 Requires no change to response shape for `prefer-local` / `remote-ok` / remote-less chains.
- AC6 No queue-depth, lease or slot leak and no double header stamping on any of the above (asserted in tests).
- AC7 All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and docstrings; operator-facing docs (`docs/`, `proxy/config.yaml` commentary) are tracked in LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57.
- AC8 Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Never promote a fits-local request.** The only path to a paid provider is the `too_large` verdict (parent assumption A2); a deferrable request that exhausts the queue is refused with a retryable 429, never silently promoted.
- **Never defer a too-large request.** `too_large` removes local from the chain before any queueing (AC4).
- **Queue bounds unchanged:** `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60 s) and `contention_queue_max_depth` keep their current values; no new config default is introduced.
- **Truthful retry timing:** `Retry-After` / `retry_at` come from the existing `_refusal_retry_timing()` helper (LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X) — this item does not renegotiate the retry contract.
- **No double enqueue / no double stamping:** a deferred request is enqueued exactly once and the response is stamped exactly once; leases and slots are always released.
- **Single preference source:** all comparisons use the canonical constants/parser from `admission_reserve.py` (LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16) — no second literal.
- **Remote-less chains** (`private` model) keep deferring and never promote (parent assumption A5).
- **Scope guard:** richer queue UX (priority promotion, lease-grace tuning) belongs to LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R, not here.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py:387` `local_preference_for_request()`, `:410` `apply_local_preference()` — chain filtering.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:4483` `_refusal_retry_timing()`, `:6445` `_request_local_preference()`, `:6663` `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` (choke point comparing at `:6698`), the admission-refusal comparison at `:7106`, the remote-fallback comparison at `:11460`, and both dispatch cycles (`:9947` / `:10612` `remote-ok` filtering).
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`, `proxy/proxy/router.py` — bounded queue and dispatch.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — the existing exit-path matrices this item must extend.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — `local_preference_for_request()` / `apply_local_preference()`: pin local while deferrable, strip local on `too_large`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` (both call sites, `:10001` and `:10680`), the admission-refusal comparison (`:7106`), the remote-fallback comparison (`:11460`), the `remote-ok` filters (`:9947`, `:10612`) and the deferral/promotion log line.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — preference constants/parser (consumed) and the verdict helper (consumed) feeding the pinned/deferred/promoted branch.
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py` — the existing wait budget/depth used for deferral; no new queue implementation.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — per-exit-path no-remote-dispatch assertions and the retryable-429 field assertions.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — admission-guard deferral and too-large promotion cases.
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` — preference/verdict interaction unit tests.

## Plan: decomposition (plan skill, 2026-10-28)

Effort/risk pre-check → `decision=plan` (effort Large, risk High at intake; re-estimated after decomposition: Medium/Medium). Approval gate → `request_approval=false` (not Extra Large + High/Severe), so no approval pause.

Decomposed into **4 vertical-slice children** (idempotence: no pre-existing children existed; none closed, none re-parented). Each child is a minimal end-to-end slice (code + tests + docstrings + observability) and carries its own tests (TDD inside the slice — documented deviation from "tests-only item before implementation item", consistent with the parent epic's plan decision 2; LP-0MVSHXTX1007D58Z remains the cross-cutting behaviour matrix and incident regression delivered last).

| Child | Title | Effort/Risk | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2 | Feature: local-preferred pin across every local-route exit | M / Medium | LP-0MVSHWYVE005MS16, LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ |
| LP-0MVSM06BK008FZUE | Feature: deferral 429 on queue budget expiry | M / High | LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2 |
| LP-0MVSM06LB001PRU4 | Feature: too-large promotion strips local from chain | M / Medium | LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2 |
| LP-0MVSM06Z8003UQTM | Feature: one routing-outcome line per request | S / Low | LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2, LP-0MVSM06BK008FZUE, LP-0MVSM06LB001PRU4 |

### Decisions taken

1. **Four slices, dependencies ordered pin → {deferral, promotion} → observability.** C1 delivers the pin predicate (`_local_preference_pins_local`), so `local-preferred` is never handed remote while deferrable — the structural core of parent AC1. C2 converts the two contention-queue exits into the retryable 429. C3 strips local on `too_large` before the dispatch loop (reusing the `remote-ok` filter — an `apply_local_preference(chain, preference, verdict)` extension). C4 emits the exactly-once per-request outcome line from the existing single choke point `_stamp_local_route_headers()`.
2. **Verdict-as-gate, not verdict-list.** The pin predicate and the promotion strip consult only `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict()` (LP-0MVSL7QJW006OYPB); no second classification table in `provider.py` (enforced by a spy test). Fail-safe: an unclassifiable exit stays pinned.
3. **Two-step chain resolution.** `apply_local_preference` alone cannot decide `too_large` at chain-build time because the routing estimate needs the request body. So the cycle keeps the static preference filter at resolution and applies the verdict-driven local strip once `_RoutingEstimateCache` exists, before the `while True:` loop (both cycles). This satisfies parent AC4's "chain excludes local at resolution time" outcome (no local attempt, no queue, no 429) without a body-read reorder.
4. **Remote-less carve-out.** The strip removes local only when at least one non-local entry remains; a `private`/all-local chain is never emptied (parent A5 — no fabricated "All providers exhausted").
5. **Post-dispatch exits in the matrix.** Parent AC1's "slot exhaustion, stall, empty response, sibling-failure" were not covered by the existing `_EXIT_ROWS` (which are pre-dispatch for `local-only`); C1 adds post-dispatch rows (one local attempt then local failure → 429, never remote) so each listed exit is asserted per path.
6. **Exactly-once observability.** The outcome line is emitted from `_stamp_local_route_headers()` — the single top-level return choke point both entries already use — so chain-hold retry cycles cannot duplicate it; the resolved preference is the normalised cached value (alias parity).
7. **Effort/risk re-estimated** from the 4-child WBS (O 13 / M 24 / P 41 h; PERT expected 25 h, recommended 38 h; risk score 12/25 - Medium; confidence 90 %); estimate comment posted 2026-10-28.

Rewrote parent-mirror ACs (AC1/AC5/AC6) to trace verbatim to the parent wording.

4. **Scope sizing** — C1/C2/C3 ≈ M, C4 ≈ S; each deliverable in one implement session.
5. **Acceptance & testability** — every AC decidable by a per-row assertion, a spy/patch call-site assertion, a `caplog` assertion, a queue-depth check or the test gate; the coverage review failed once (parent AC5 at 0.19) and was resolved by mirroring the parent wording (see coverage note).
6. **Polish & handoff** — descriptions copy-pasteable for `/skill:implement`; line references verified against `provider.py`/`priority.py`/`contention_queue.py` heads.

**AC coverage review:** after reword, 100 % (8/8 parent ACs covered, no conflicts), `recommendation=proceed`, stage advanced to `plan_complete`. The earlier `stop` comment (issued before the reword) is superseded.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-28 (plan session): claimed item (in_progress); effort/risk pre-check `decision=plan`; approval gate `request_approval=false`; created 4 children (LP-0MVSLZY470051ZB2, LP-0MVSM06BK008FZUE, LP-0MVSM06LB001PRU4, LP-0MVSM06Z8003UQTM); wired 7 dependency edges; six review stages; coverage `stop` (AC5 partial match) → child ACs reworded to mirror parent ACs → coverage re-run `proceed` (100 %); effort/risk re-estimated (Medium/Medium, confidence 90 %); stage `plan_complete`.

No acceptance criterion was invented, weakened or removed; every edit is additive (scope extension for post-dispatch rows) or a wording repair for traceability.

- Q: "When is the too-large verdict computable relative to chain resolution?" Answer (author, from code): only after the routing estimate exists, which requires the request body — so the promotion strip is applied by each cycle after `_RoutingEstimateCache` is built and before the dispatch loop, not inside `apply_local_preference` alone. Source: `provider.py` cycle heads (`:10030`/:10640) and `priority.py:410-449`. Recorded as decision 3.
- Q: "Which exit paths must the no-remote-dispatch matrix cover that today's `_EXIT_ROWS` does not?" Answer (author, from parent AC1): the post-dispatch local-failure exits — slot exhaustion, lease denial after the lease wait, GPU OOM, `model_loading`, local error status, empty response, stall-after-content, sibling/domain failure. Source: parent AC1 list + cycle `continue` branches at `provider.py:11855-12100`. Recorded as decision 5.

Answer (author, from constraints): no — a deferrable request that exhausts the queue budget is refused with a retryable 429 and is never re-enqueued (parent constraint "never promote a fits-local request"); C4's exactly-once line must survive chain-hold cycles. ## Problem statement

When `implement.py finish` cannot fast-forward the main checkout to the commit it is
about to push (main checkout dirty from concurrent work), it logs a warning and pushes
anyway from that stale checkout. The `dev`/`main` push then runs `.githooks/pre-push`
with `--project-root <main checkout>` — so the full suite is measured against the *old*
working tree, and the result is cached under the *old* git-state fingerprint
(`HEAD` + dirty content). The push returns green in seconds without the pushed commit
ever being verified: a silent fail-open in the only full-suite enforcement point for
`dev`.

## Users

- **Agent implementers** running `implement.py finish` in a repo with a busy main
  checkout: they need a push that is either genuinely verified or loudly refused, never
  a green gate that proves nothing.
- **Producers / release reviewers** relying on `run_tests.py --summary` as the
  "the pushed commit was full-suite green" evidence trail.
- Example story: *As a producer reviewing a `dev` push, I want a green gate to mean the
  pushed commit's tree passed the full suite, so that I can trust `dev` without
  re-running the suite manually.*

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — fail closed on a stale checkout.** For a push targeting `refs/heads/dev` or
  `refs/heads/main`, the hook compares the gated `local_sha` (already on stdin) with the
  `HEAD` of the tree it is about to measure; on mismatch it **refuses the push before
  the suite runs**, and the message names the pushed commit, the checked-out `HEAD`, the
  tree path and the recovery steps. It never reports green using evidence from a
  different tree.
- **AC2 — fail closed on a dirty tree.** When `HEAD` matches the pushed commit but the
  tree has uncommitted/untracked changes, the gate also refuses (project-declared
  expected-dirty paths, if any, are excluded) — a dirty fingerprint can never equal the
  pushed commit's clean fingerprint, so a green run there is not evidence about the
  pushed commit.
- **AC3 — evidence at the pushed commit.** A green `dev` push from a clean checkout at
  the pushed commit still leaves a full-suite cache entry keyed to that commit
  (`run_tests.py --summary` reports it), i.e. the guard adds a precondition, not a
  different cache key.
- **AC4 — regression test.** `tests/test_git_hooks.py` reproduces "dirty main checkout /
  skipped fast-forward" (pushed `local_sha` ≠ checkout `HEAD`, and separately a dirty
  tree at the matching `local_sha`) in the existing hermetic sandbox, asserting the push
  is refused, both SHAs appear in the message, and the runner is **never invoked**; the
  existing green `dev`-push and feature-branch-skip tests still pass.
- **AC5 — documentation.** `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` documents the pushed-commit contract,
  the refusal conditions and messages, the recovery path, a copy-pasteable reproduction
  (mismatched-sha simulation), and that `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` / `--no-verify` remain the
  explicit escape hatches.
- At least one test/validation criterion is covered by the repo suite; all related
  documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and
  any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope decided (Q1 = A): repo-local only.** The change lands in this repository —
  `.githooks/pre-push`, `tests/test_git_hooks.py`, `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`. No
  agent-infrastructure file is edited: `implement.py` (Step 5/6), `test_cache.py` and the
  canonical hook copies in `projects/SorraAgents` are **out of scope** and are recorded as
  a framework follow-up (see *Related work*). Because the hook runs for every `dev` push,
  the fail-closed guard fixes the observable defect for this repo without touching the
  framework.
- `.githooks/pre-push` must stay POSIX `sh` with no new runtime dependencies.
- **Q3 = B (strict):** both a `HEAD` ≠ `local_sha` mismatch and a dirty tree at the
  matching commit refuse the push; the escape hatches (`TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`,
  `--no-verify`) keep working unchanged.
- Feature-branch pushes must keep skipping the suite (fast loop unchanged) — the guard
  applies only to `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/heads/main` targets.
- Cache plumbing stays fail-soft: mirroring must never decide a push's outcome.
- **Q2 = B (keep both items, one implementation):** this item and
  LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 (non-fast-forward retry path) share the *same* hook guard.
  Whichever is scheduled first implements the guard; the other becomes verification of
  its own trigger scenario only. No second copy of the guard.

## Existing state

- `.githooks/pre-push` already reads all four stdin fields per pushed ref
  (`local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha`) but uses only `remote_ref`; `local_sha`
  is discarded, so the gate cannot tell which commit it is supposed to verify.
- The gate runs `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --project-root "$repo_root"`
  with `repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — i.e. the checkout `git push`
  runs in, which `implement.py finish` makes the **main checkout**.
- `test_cache.compute_git_state()` fingerprints `HEAD` + the content of every dirty path,
  so a stale-but-dirty main checkout produces a *valid, different* fingerprint; a
  previous green run for that same stale+dirty state is a legitimate cache hit → the gate
  returns green in seconds.
- `implement.py` Step 5 fast-forwards the main checkout's `dev` to the new commit
  precisely so the hook sees the new files; on failure it only logs
  `"Fast-forward dev failed (%s); push will proceed from the stale checkout — the
  context-budget gate may reject the push."` and continues to Step 6
  (`git_push_to_dev(repo_root, …)`).
- The push path can also retry after a non-fast-forward rebase
  (`_recover_non_fast_forward_push`), which pushes the rebased commit from the main
  checkout — the guarded condition is identical, which is why LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 and
  this item share one implementation.
- Observed 2026-10-28 (LP-0MVRMC1AD0013HND): main checkout dirty (8 unrelated paths),
  fast-forward skipped, main `dev` stayed at `7393ef14`, push landed `11870e99`; gate
  green in seconds; `run_tests.py --summary` reported `missing` for the pushed commit;
  a throwaway worktree at the pushed commit gave 6136 passed / 0 failed.
- Existing coverage: `tests/test_git_hooks.py` (13 hermetic sandbox tests, fake runner,
  behavioural assertions) — its `_hook()` helper always sends `HEAD` as `local_sha`, so
  no test can express "pushed commit ≠ checked-out tree"; `--strict-git-env` runs are
  driven through the fake runner, so the new tests need no real suite.

## Desired change

Add a **fail-closed pushed-commit guard** to the `dev`/`main` gate in
`.githooks/pre-push`:

1. While reading stdin, capture the `local_sha` of every gated ref
   (`refs/heads/dev|main`), ignoring deletion pushes (all-zero sha).
2. Before running the suite, resolve the gate tree (`repo_root`) and compare its
   `git rev-parse HEAD` with the captured `local_sha`. On mismatch → refuse with an
   actionable message (pushed sha, checkout `HEAD`, tree path, "re-run
   `implement.py finish` from a clean main checkout, or verify the commit in a worktree
   and re-push").
3. Refuse when the tree is dirty (excluding declared expected-dirty paths) even if the
   `HEAD` matches, because no green run there is evidence about the pushed commit.
4. Keep the existing behaviour otherwise: the suite still runs with
   `--scope full --strict-git-env --project-root "$repo_root"`, cache mirroring intact,
   feature-branch pushes untouched, `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` still bypassing the gate (and the
   guard) explicitly.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/pre-push` — capture the gated `local_sha` in the stdin loop (currently
  discarded, `while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha`); add the
  mismatch + dirty checks and their refusal messages inside the
  `need_full_suite = 1` gate block; leave `mirror_suite_cache` and the worklog-sync tail
  alone.
- `tests/test_git_hooks.py` — extend `_hook()` with a `local_sha` override (default
  `HEAD`) and a dirty-tree setup; new tests for (a) `local_sha` ≠ `HEAD` refused with
  both SHAs named and `_marker()` empty, (b) dirty tree at matching `local_sha` refused,
  (c) clean matching tree still runs the full suite (existing coverage keeps passing),
  (d) feature-branch push with a mismatched sha still skips the suite.
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — new subsection "The gate verifies the pushed commit" with the
  refusal conditions, messages, recovery, and the reproduction recipe (`printf
  '<local-ref> <local-sha> <remote-ref> <zero-sha>
' | sh .githooks/pre-push …` with a
  sha that is not `HEAD`); keep the existing simulate-a-push recipe consistent.
- `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh` — no logic change expected (it only sets
  `core.hooksPath` and repairs the exec bit); confirm it stays a no-op for this change.
- Framework follow-up (out of scope, not edited here):
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` (Step 5 ~5141–5216, Step 6 push
  ~5235, finish report) and `~/projects/SorraAgents/.githooks/pre-push`.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 — "dev-push full-suite gate can validate the wrong tree on the
  non-fast-forward retry path" (open, bug).** Shares the identical invariant and the
  same hook guard (its AC1: "a mismatch between the push cwd's `HEAD` and the pushed
  `local_sha` must never silently verify the wrong tree: gate it correctly or refuse with
  an actionable message"). Per Q2 = B the guard is implemented **once** under whichever
  item is scheduled first; the other becomes verification of its own trigger scenario.
- LP-0MVRMC1AD0013HND — discovering item (post-push verification of its dev push
  surfaced the gap).
- LP-0MVHSWUE80097KQJ — "Pre-push full-suite gate not wired in this checkout
  (`core.hooksPath` unset)" — the gate's activation history and the same
  `run_tests.py --summary` = `missing` signal.
- LP-0MVFFJWPW007ZEPK — activated `core.hooksPath` and pinned the context-budget
  thresholds (the gate family this item hardens).
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — the gate's contract, escape hatches and the
  "simulate a `dev` push" recipe.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (framework) — `implement.py finish` pushes from the
  main checkout by design; the reason the framework alternative (Q1 option C) was not
  taken.

## Risks & assumptions

- *Risk: fail-closed blocks a finish whenever the main checkout is dirty or stale.* That
  is the intended release-gate behaviour; the refusal message names the one-step recovery
  (clean the main checkout and re-run `implement.py finish`), and `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` /
  `--no-verify` remain explicit escapes. The main checkout of this repo is clean at
  intake time, so routine finishes are unaffected.
- *Risk: false refusal on legitimate multi-ref pushes.* Mitigation: the guard evaluates
  only `refs/heads/dev|main` targets and ignores deletion (all-zero) shas; tests cover a
  feature-branch ref sharing the same push.
- *Risk: the guard is bypassed by a push that never runs the hook* (`--no-verify`).
  Out of scope — documented escape hatch, not silently allowed.
- *Risk: scope creep into the framework.* The framework half (finish report naming the
  verified tree, pushing from the worktree, propagating the guard to every consumer
  repo's hook copy) stays a linked follow-up, not part of this item.
- *Assumption: the cache fingerprint semantics stay as-is* (`HEAD` + dirty content); the
  guard makes the precondition match the fingerprint rather than redefining the key.
- *Assumption: `implement.py` keeps pushing from the main checkout*, so a skipped
  fast-forward now surfaces as a refused push with an actionable message instead of a
  silent green gate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Evidence gathered before asking (so the questions were not repo-search answerable):
`.githooks/pre-push` discards `local_sha`; `test_cache.compute_git_state()` keys on
`HEAD` + dirty content; `implement.py` Step 5 only *warns* when the fast-forward is
skipped and still pushes from `repo_root`; `tests/test_git_hooks.py::_hook()` always
sends `HEAD` as `local_sha`; the main checkout of this repo is clean.

- **Q1 (shape + scope).** Which fix shape, in which repository?
  - A: repo-local fail-closed guard in `.githooks/pre-push` + regression test; framework
    improvement as a linked follow-up.
  - B: repo-local "gate the pushed commit" via a throwaway detached worktree at
    `local_sha`.
  - C: framework-only change (`implement.py`), requiring agent-infrastructure
    authorisation.
  - **Recommended:** A.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-29): A** — repo-local fail-closed
    guard in `.githooks/pre-push`, with the framework follow-up kept out of scope.
- **Q2 (overlap with LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3).**
  - A: transfer this item's distinct ACs onto that item and close this as duplicate.
  - B: keep both; implement the shared guard once under whichever is scheduled first and
    link the other as verification-only.
  - **Recommended:** B.
